subsystems.name: Pressure hull and buoyancy
subsystems.role: survives the crushing pressure of a deep ocean and keeps the vehicle neutrally buoyant.

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: sets the range; with no cable and no sunlight, everything comes from a battery or a radioisotope source.
parts: lithium primary or rechargeable battery pack

subsystems.name: Navigation
subsystems.role: finds the way with no GPS and no line of sight to the surface.

subsystems.name: Autonomy and communication
subsystems.role: plans and reacts on its own, because a radio link through ice and water is impossible.

subsystems.name: Science payload
subsystems.role: measures the water and maps the underside of the ice.

subsystems.name: Docking and recharge station
subsystems.role: the fixed point the vehicle returns to for power, data and sample handover.

buildSteps.title: Define the mission
buildSteps.detail: Choose the target ocean, ice thickness, required range in kilometres and the measurements that justify the trip.

buildSteps.title: Design the pressure hull
buildSteps.detail: Size a sphere or cylinder for the target depth — tens of megapascals on Europa — and add buoyancy foam so the vehicle hovers rather than sinks.

buildSteps.title: Integrate power and propulsion
buildSteps.detail: Fit the battery pack and thrusters, then calculate the range that energy budget allows at cruising speed.

buildSteps.title: Build the navigation stack
buildSteps.detail: Combine inertial dead reckoning with sonar and Doppler velocity logs, and prove drift stays small over a long run.

buildSteps.title: Write the autonomy software
buildSteps.detail: Encode the mission, contingency behaviours and safe-mode returns so the vehicle can complete a survey without being driven.

buildSteps.title: Test in tanks and open water
buildSteps.detail: Bench tests, then lake and coastal trials, then increasingly long autonomous runs.

buildSteps.title: Prove it under real ice
buildSteps.detail: Deploy through a hole in an ice shelf or glacier, navigate for tens of kilometres away from any beacon, sense the water and return — the Antarctic analogue campaign.

buildSteps.title: Add docking and sample handling
buildSteps.detail: Practise returning to a fixed station, recharging and transferring samples and data automatically.

buildSteps.title: Harden for the target world
buildSteps.detail: Qualify electronics for Jupiter's radiation, years of cruise and the extreme cold, then integrate with a cryobot or lander that delivers it through the ice.

prerequisites.why: under-ice vehicles must fix their position from inertial sensors and sonar alone; drift over long runs is still the key limit.

prerequisites.tech: High energy-density power for cold, dark environments
prerequisites.why: range is set directly by battery capacity, since recharging depends on returning to a station.
something must get the vehicle through kilometres of ice shell to reach the ocean.
radio cannot cross water or thick ice, so data and commands travel as slow acoustic packets.
reaching an icy moon's surface with a heavy payload has been studied but not yet flown.
electronics near Jupiter must survive the radiation environment of the inner Jovian system.

pathway.milestone: Antarctic analogue vehicles (such as Icefin and ARTEMIS) survey beneath ice shelves and glacier grounding lines
pathway.unlocks: the operational model: untethered under-ice range, chemical sensing and sample return.

pathway.milestone: Europa Clipper (launched 2024) and ESA's JUICE characterise the ice shell, ocean and plumes
pathway.unlocks: the data needed to choose a landing site and design the vehicle.

pathway.milestone: a cryobot plus AUV demonstrated end-to-end through a thick ice shelf or glacier
pathway.unlocks: confidence that melting through and swimming free can work as one system.

pathway.milestone: a lander mission that melts through the shell and releases an autonomous explorer
pathway.unlocks: direct sampling of an alien ocean — the only way to test it for habitability.
